Package dyntabs.ai

Class SpeakBuilder

java.lang.Object
dyntabs.ai.SpeakBuilder
public class SpeakBuilder extends Object
Turns text into spoken audio — the outbound half of the voice channel.

The shortest useful form


 Speech speech = EasyAI.speak().from("Order ORD-004 has been delivered.");
 return Response.ok(speech.bytes()).type(speech.mimeType()).build();

Model, voice, key and base URL come from easyai.properties, defaulting to your chat settings — so, as with ListenBuilder, the common case needs no new configuration (see VoiceConfig).

Server-side speech vs. the browser's own

A browser can already speak text for free via the Web Speech API, and for a desktop app that is often the right answer. Synthesizing on the server earns its keep when you need a consistent voice across browsers and devices, a language the client has no voice installed for, or audio you can store, attach and replay — a recorded confirmation, an accessibility narration, an outbound notification. This is the path for those; it returns the bytes and leaves playback entirely up to you.

Overriding per call


 Speech speech = EasyAI.speak()
                       .withModel("tts-1-hd")
                       .withVoice("nova")
                       .withEventListener(e -> log.info("{}", e))
                       .from(answer);

Analogy: a voice-over artist. You hand over the script and get back a recording — the artist neither writes the script nor decides when it is played.
